svg.title: Root cutover sequence and the point of no return
svg.desc: On receiving a typed reconfiguration item the owner loop submits pending rows as a packed OutputBatch, flushes and closes the old OutputWriter, and reaches the point of no return. Only afterwards does the owner validate the frontier and resolved interfaces, compile the replacement, transfer context, install candidate identities, close and reopen the input generation, open a fresh writer from the resolved output interface, install active state, and send the acknowledgement. Any failure after the old writer closes terminates the owner loop because the old external interface no longer exists.
svg.text: Root cutover: drain first, then everything that can fail
Committed old output is still reachable
1 receive typed Reconfigure(MonitorConfig)
already parsed by the transport adapter; no decoding here
2 flush pending engine rows
3 flush and close the old OutputWriter
writer completion is the old-generation handoff barrier
point of no return — the old writer is closed
No rollback — any failure below terminates the owner loop
5 validate frontier and resolved interfaces
6 compile the replacement specification
7 transfer context, if requested
8 install candidate monitor identities
9 close old input, open replacement input
10 open fresh OutputWriter from resolved interface
11 install active I/O state and replacement engine
12 send ReconfigurationAck
last: cutover/open complete, not future publish success
Steps 1–3 run for every recognized command, including one whose replacement later proves invalid, so accepted rows
reach the writer handoff where possible. A failure before step 3 is still terminal; it simply has not yet discarded the old interface.
